issues.title: Tailwind classes in incorrect order
issues.description: Tailwind utility classes must follow standard ordering: layout, positioning, sizing, spacing (margin before padding), typography, visual effects. The classes have padding (pr-2) before margin (mt-[-16px]), which violates this convention.
issues.rule_name: Tailwind CSS Classes Must Follow Standard Ordering

issues.title: Missing optional chaining causes runtime error when openForm is undefined
issues.description: The code accesses `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but openForm can be undefined when rendering certain forms (like the main comment form). The original code correctly used `openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet` with optional chaining. This will cause a "Cannot read property 'in_reply_to_snippet' of undefined" runtime error when the FormWrapper is rendered without an openForm prop, crashing the component.

issues.title: Editor editability incorrectly depends on member expertise instead of name
issues.description: The Form component determines whether the editor should be editable by checking `member?.expertise` instead of `memberName` (which is derived from `member?.name`). According to the comment and the original logic, the editor should be disabled only when the member doesn't have a name or when submitting. Expertise is optional metadata, but name is required for posting. This bug prevents users without expertise from typing in the comment editor, even though they have a valid name and should be allowed to comment.

issues.title: Reply threading broken for nested comments due to incorrect in_reply_to_id
issues.description: The submit function uses `parent.id` as `in_reply_to_id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. For nested replies (replying to a reply), these values differ: `openForm.in_reply_to_id` points to the specific comment being replied to, while `parent.id` points to the top-level parent comment. Using `parent.id` breaks the reply chain, causing nested replies to be incorrectly threaded to the wrong comment. This destroys the conversation hierarchy and makes it impossible to track which comment a user is actually replying to in multi-level discussions.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25858 - 🐛 Fixed reply form showing parent comment author's details

structured_output.summary:
The PR's stated goal is a good fix. The reply form header should show the logged-in member's own name and expertise, not fall back to the details of the comment being replied to. Removing the `comment?.member?.*` fallbacks in `Form` and `FormWrapper` and dropping the `comment` prop from `FormWrapper` does that correctly.

The diff also changes three things the description doesn't mention, and each one breaks something:
1. The editor's editable gate now checks `member.expertise` instead of `memberName`. Expertise is optional, so members without it can no longer type comments.
2. `ReplyForm` now always sends `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`. That discards the reply-to-reply target and tags every direct reply as replying to the top-level comment.
3. The optional chaining on `openForm` in `FormWrapper` was removed. `MainForm` never passes `openForm`, so focusing the main comment box throws a TypeError, and the line also fails strict TypeScript.

These need to be reverted before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The core fallback removal is right, but the PR also adds three regressions. Members without expertise can't comment, reply-to-reply threading is broken, and the main form crashes when opened. Fixing each one is a one-line revert.

architecture.overview:
In comments-ui, `Comment` renders a `ReplyFormBox` → `ReplyForm` whenever an `OpenCommentForm` of type `reply` matches it. `openReplyForm` in `comment.tsx` builds that `OpenCommentForm` and sets `in_reply_to_id`/`in_reply_to_snippet` only when the user is replying to a reply. `ReplyForm` and `MainForm` both wrap the shared `Form` in `FormWrapper`. `FormWrapper` renders the member header (avatar, name, expertise button) and opens the `addDetailsPopup`. `Form` controls whether the TipTap editor is editable.

The PR takes the parent `Comment` out of the header path: `FormWrapper` no longer gets a `comment` prop, and both components read name and expertise only from `useAppContext().member`. It also changes how `ReplyForm` builds the `addReply` payload (it now uses `parent.id`), switches the editable gate in `Form` to check expertise, and removes the optional chaining on `openForm` in `FormWrapper`.
steps: Start in `comment.tsx` `openReplyForm`: it dispatches `openCommentForm` with an `OpenCommentForm`, and sets `in_reply_to_id` only when replying to a nested reply.
`ReplyFormBox` renders `ReplyForm` with `parent` set to the top-level comment and the `openForm` above.
`ReplyForm.submit` dispatches `addReply`. In `actions.ts`, `addReply` sets `parent_id` and calls `api.comments.add`. This PR changes the `in_reply_to_id` sent there.
`FormWrapper` (shared by `ReplyForm` and `MainForm`) renders the member name and expertise header. This PR removes the parent-comment fallback here.
`Form` sets whether the editor is editable from member state and submit progress. This PR changes the condition from name to expertise.

findings.title: Editor is now read-only for any member without expertise
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx, the useEffect in `Form` (around lines 259-265) now calls `editor.setEditable(!!member?.expertise && ...)`. That makes the editor read-only for members without expertise, which is an optional field. Restore the original gate `!!memberName && progress !== 'sending'` and set the dependency array back to `[editor, memberName, progress]`. Then add or confirm an e2e test showing that a member with a name and no expertise can type and submit a comment.

findings.title: Reply-to-reply target lost: in_reply_to_id is always the top-level parent
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx, the `submit` callback (lines 24-35) now sends `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`. `parent` is always the top-level comment, so the reply-to-reply target that `openReplyForm` stores in `openForm.in_reply_to_id` (comment.tsx ~line 110) is lost. Direct replies also get an in_reply_to_id they shouldn't have. Revert to `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` and add `openForm` back to the useCallback deps. Then run the 'Can reply to a reply' e2e tests in test/e2e/actions.test.ts.

findings.title: Removed optional chaining crashes MainForm when it opens
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx, line 313 in `FormWrapper` dereferences `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining. `openForm` is optional, and MainForm (main-form.tsx line 98) never passes it, so the main comment form throws once it opens. Restore `!!openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet`, then confirm `tsc --noEmit` passes for apps/comments-ui.

findings.title: Name test only asserts what's absent, not what's shown
findings.fixPrompt: In apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts, the test 'Reply form does not inherit name from parent comment author' (~lines 650-680) only asserts `not.toHaveText('Named Author')`. That can pass even if the element is missing. Check what FormWrapper in src/components/content/forms/form.tsx renders for a member with no name, assert that exact output (placeholder text or the add-name prompt), and assert the editor isn't editable.

findings.title: Removing the parent-comment fallback is the right fix
findings.body:
The original bug was that `member?.name ?? comment?.member?.name` showed another user's identity in your own reply header. Taking the `comment` prop off `FormWrapper` entirely, instead of patching around it, means the header can no longer pick up the parent author's details by accident. The new expertise test reproduces the reported bug well: it checks that the parent shows 'Head of Comments' and that the reply header doesn't.
